findings.title: The ten-slot recovery budget is now spent on sidecars the old code filtered out first, so ten unreadable or id-less sidecars blind the belt entirely
findings.evidence: origin/main's intake.mjs:436-437 filtered BEFORE the slice: `const rows = (await listIntakeMetas()).filter((row) => row && !row.corrupt && row.intakeId); for (const meta of rows.slice(0, 10))`. HEAD's intake.mjs:479-481 slices FIRST and filters inside the loop: `const settled = (await listEntries()).filter(...); for (const entry of settled.slice(0, RECOVERY_BATCH)) { const meta = await entry.read(); if (!meta || meta.corrupt || !meta.intakeId) continue; ... }`. A {corrupt} marker, a null (ENOENT between listing and read) and a body with no intakeId each consume one of the ten slots. PROVEN read-only on this rig against the built modules: with 12 unparseable intake-<uuid>.json sidecars sorting ahead of one genuinely recoverable sidecar (all mtimes aged 10 minutes), recoverPendingDocumentIntakes returned {"recovered":0,"deferred":0,"expired":0} - the recoverable intake was never opened; the pre-#966 loop head run against the SAME directory reached it (OLD belt would reach: ["ffffffff-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]). Starvation is PERMANENT when the junk sidecars do not match sweepSpoolTtl's strict name regex ^intake-[0-9a-f-]{36}\.(?:bin|json)$ (spool.mjs:430): with ten files named intake-00junk-N.json, listIntakeMetaEntries() listed 11 entries, the belt returned all zeroes, and sweepSpoolTtl() removed only the legitimate uuid-named sidecar (spoolRemoved: 1, still listed: 10). Even with uuid-shaped names the blind window is the spool TTL - minimum 15 minutes, 60 by default (spoolConfig). No cell covers it: p966.budget and 'p966.quiet ... BUDGET' both fill the budget with status:"uploading" bodies, i.e. entries that ARE read successfully, so they exercise the budget but never the corrupt/null arm.
findings.user_impact: A crashed mid-flight intake is never resumed - the human's uploaded document silently never appears - for as long as ten unreadable sidecars sit ahead of it in readdir order, and nothing is logged. packages/runtime/README.md's claim that 'a spool full of live uploads cannot starve the belt of the crashed intake behind them' is true only for live uploads.
findings.required_fix: Take RECOVERY_BATCH from ACTIONABLE metas, not from raw entries: keep reading settled entries until ten usable metas have been handled, under a separate larger cap on opens (e.g. 3x), or restore the pre-slice filter over a bounded read window. Add a cell: >=10 corrupt/id-less entries ahead of one recoverable entry, assert it is still reached. Consider logging a corrupt sidecar once instead of skipping it silently, and/or widening sweepSpoolTtl's regex so unparseable intake-*.json files are reaped.

findings.title: p966.expire passes only because under five seconds elapse since p966.race - the cells share one spool directory and the race cell never cleans up
findings.evidence: intake-sidecar-race.test.mjs sets ONE CLARA_SPOOL_DIR for the whole file (before hook, ~line 41) and p966.race leaves intake-<id>.json behind with status "spooled" and expiresAt now+15min - i.e. actionable. p966.expire (line 219) uses the DEFAULT listEntries, i.e. the real directory, and asserts assert.equal(calls.length, 1). That holds only while the race fixture's mtime is still inside the 5 s quiet window. Proven by shortening the window, which does not touch p966.expire's own subject (that cell ages its own sidecar 60 s with utimes, so the guard is irrelevant to it): `CLARA_INTAKE_SIDECAR_QUIET_MS=1 node --test tests/intake-sidecar-race.test.mjs` -> `not ok 7 - p966.expire ... Expected values to be strictly equal: 2 !== 1`, with the stray side effect printed: `[clara-runtime] intake FAILED intake=be2a3770-... code=internal canonicalReached=false detail=canonical intake metadata is incomplete`. Baseline (no env) is 10/10 only because cells 4-6 are pure in-memory doubles that finish in ~20 ms. Any stall over five seconds between p966.race and p966.expire - a loaded ten-lane rig, a slower CI box, the whole-runtime-suite run - reds a gate cell for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
findings.required_fix: Give the filesystem cells their own spool directory (mkdtemp per cell, or set CLARA_SPOOL_DIR inside each cell), or have p966.race remove its sidecar (removeIntakeSpool) in a t.after. Do not let the quiet window double as cell isolation.
findings.note: intake-db.test.mjs's p966 cell also reds under CLARA_INTAKE_SIDECAR_QUIET_MS=1, but that is the lane's own declared vacuity control (its `live` sweep asserts the guard), not this defect; the other eleven db cells stayed green.

findings.title: renameIntoPlace converts a persistent EPERM into a two-second stall on every sidecar write, on the latency-sensitive intake path, with no cell
findings.evidence: spool.mjs:57-59 sets RENAME_RETRY_MS = 2000 and the loop at :81-92 retries EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY until the deadline. MEASURED read-only on this rig: with one open(meta,'r') handle deliberately held (a stuck AV/backup/indexer handle - and #693 already shows Defender holding files on this host), writeIntakeMeta returned `EPERM after 2003 ms` instead of failing immediately. Every intake status transition goes through atomicJson, so a stuck handle costs ~2 s per transition per intake, multiplied across a 100-child batch - the exact workload #636/#966 were measured on. No cell asserts the give-up path, its latency, or the knob; the suite's only timing assertion (p966.race) exercises the SUCCEEDING retry. The repo's own intake-e2e.mjs:254 cell is a latency assertion on this path.
findings.required_fix: Either lower the default deadline to the order of the contended window (e.g. 250 ms, still ~100x a reader's handle) or make it caller-supplied so a live request keeps a short budget while the belt keeps a long one. Add a cell pinning the give-up: a held handle -> the ORIGINAL EPERM is thrown, the temp file is gone, and it happens within the deadline.

findings.title: The chat-clarify belt no longer runs when the heartbeat fails - an untested behaviour change
findings.evidence: Before: leader.mjs called reconcileChatClarifies in its own try/catch BEFORE runReconcilerSweep, so a heartbeat failure did not stop it. Now reconciler.mjs:737-744 returns {heartbeatOk:false, beltErrors:["heartbeat"]} before reaching the belt at :755. The lane states the rationale in its report and in the module comment ('nothing that breaks that single-row upsert would spare a belt on the same connection'), which is reasonable, and the ticket's criterion ('the belt still runs before the rest of the sweep') is satisfied - but it is an untested change of behaviour on a belt whose whole job is settling conversations a crash left parked.
findings.required_fix: None required. If kept, say it in the README's Order paragraph (it currently says only 'immediately after the heartbeat') so the next reader does not rediscover it during an incident.

findings.title: The operator log string for a chat-clarify belt failure changed, while the wrapper's comment claims pre-existing names are preserved verbatim
findings.evidence: Old (leader.mjs, removed): `[reconcile] chat clarify belt error: <msg>`. New (reconciler.mjs:709, via belt("chat clarify reconcile")): `[reconcile] chat clarify reconcile error: <msg>`. The belt wrapper's comment at reconciler.mjs:706-707 says the idiom and 'the three pre-existing names' are preserved 'so an operator's existing log greps keep matching' - that guarantee does not extend to this fourth name. chat-clarify-sweep-wiring.test.mjs pins the NEW string, so the change is deliberate and covered; only hosted greps and alerts are not.
findings.required_fix: Orchestrator: check whether any hosted alert or saved search matches 'chat clarify belt error' before release. No code change needed.

findings.title: 'the counters are positive evidence that the belt ran' overstates the receipt, and the counter cell exercises only the dormant path
findings.evidence: packages/runtime/README.md (#852 section): 'a FAILED belt contributes no counters at all, so "chatClarifyResumed" in swept is positive evidence that the belt ran.' reconciler-chat-clarify.mjs:191-203 returns the ZEROED counter bag and issues no statement at all when resumeHook is not a function, and again when hasDeliveryColumns() is false - so the five keys appear on the receipt in both dormant cases. chat-clarify-sweep-wiring.test.mjs's '#852 receipt: ... all FIVE chat-clarify counters' uses sweepClient() with the default deliveryColumns = 0, i.e. it asserts the spread over exactly that dormant early return; no sweep cell drives a resting row through the belt (that coverage lives in control-chat-clarify.test.mjs, against the belt directly).
findings.required_fix: Soften the README sentence to 'the belt was reached and did not throw', or add a sweep cell with deliveryColumns=3 and one resting row so the counters come from a real pass.

findings.title: The reader half only shields sidecars quiet for under five seconds; the guarantee for a real upload rests entirely on the writer-half retry, and task sidecars did not get the reader half
findings.evidence: The quiet window is 5 s (SIDECAR_QUIET_MS) while a 20 MB upload takes longer, and mid-upload states ('uploading'/'receiving') are not in RECOVERABLE_STATES - so such a sidecar is still OPENED on every sweep and then skipped, which is the original race, mitigated only by renameIntoPlace. Separately, listTaskMetas() still bulk-opens every task-*.json on each call: health.mjs:59 (every health probe) and reconciler-documents.mjs:282 (the document-task fallback), with mergeTaskMeta writing through the same atomicJson. Those inherit the writer-half retry (correct) but not the metadata-first reader. Consistent with the ticket's scope ('the spool sidecar listing the belt uses'), so recorded rather than charged.
findings.required_fix: None for this ticket. Worth a follow-up: give listTaskMetas' callers the same lazy-entry shape, and consider expressing the quiet window against the capability lifetime rather than a flat five seconds.

No second caller of reconcileChatClarifies survives (leader.mjs neither imports nor calls it); runReconcilerSweep has exactly one production caller, leader.mjs:226, which forwards the same deps object, so resumeHook (startWorld.ts:399) still reaches the belt and deps.onlyFirm still scopes it.

The parts-parity re-fingerprint follows the documented #640/#636 precedent (the sha is of the whole normalised return statement); check-parts-parity.mjs is green and the '...deps' tuple, which belongs to a different statement, is correctly left alone.

renameIntoPlace does not swallow: only the three contention codes retry, the original error is rethrown past the deadline, and the temp file is removed before the throw so a transient write failure cannot grow the spool.

The one red in the lane's runtime run is #693 (EICAR quarantined by Defender) - reproduced here, and git diff over scan.mjs / intake-unit.test.mjs is empty, so it is not this lane's.
